messages.subject: lavaanify function causing issues.
parts:
Hello all,

I have two related issues.

First, using the lavaanify function makes it impossible for me to run my models. For example, if I run

model <- 'L =~ O1+O2+O3'
fit   <- cfa( model, data = data)

Then the model fits without issues. However, if I do

model <- 'L =~ O1+O2+O3'
lmodel <- lavaanify(model)
fit   <- cfa(lmodel, data = data)

Then I get the following message: 

Error in estimateModel(lavaanModel, samplestats = lavaanSampleStats, X = lavaanData@X,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: initial model-implied matrix (Sigma) is not positive definite;
  check your model and/or starting parameters.

How do I fix this?

Second, I want to run a CFA model in lavaan. I'm trying to free the factor loading of the first indicator of every latent variable (by default, it is set to 1). Is there a way I can do this without using the lavaanify function?

Best regards,
Guillaume

> = lavaanData@X, : /

> definite;/
> / check your model and/or starting parameters./

Please read the lavaan paper. lavaanify() is similar to the lavaan()
function: it will not 'add' anything automatically.

Try this:

lavaanify(model, auto.var = TRUE, auto.fix.single = TRUE)

which will work for this 1-factor example. See the ?cfa man page
(section Details) to learn wich auto.* flags are set if you are using
the cfa() function. As a shortcut, this will also work:

lavaanify(model, auto=TRUE, model.type="cfa")
